verdict.rationale: Google Authenticator's own docs describe a QR-code transfer that works without a Google Account, and community users confirm it exports all saved codes into one QR code. That is a real first-party export path. Community reports also say the bundled export QR may not be readable by other TOTP apps and that there is no simple text or file export, so the 'open formats and leave' part is weak. Missing for 10: documented open/standard export format (e.g., per-account otpauth URIs or a file export), confirmed interoperability with other authenticator apps, and an official data-portability or export doc.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: On your old device, create a QR code... On your new device, tap Scan QR code
If you use Google Authenticator without a Google Account, you can still manually transfer your codes to another device.
Google Authenticator has a feature to allow export of all saved codes into one QR code for re-import into Google Authenticator running on another device.
